currentPosture.specEvidence: Component-level parity lives in docs/evidence/gpui/gpui-functionality-census.json; this artifact records only broad posture and section/layer evidence.
currentPosture.limitation: This artifact does not prove broad native semantics, focus, keyboard, announcement, or assistive-technology parity.

livePlatformProofAttempt.launch: Both proof windows used the window-capture transport with focus:false. The clean window remained non-frontmost for 239 successful samples with no failed reads; the planted window remained non-frontmost for 240 successful samples with no failed reads.
verifiedSignals: A toggled Poodle Button retains its AXTitle and AXValue; accesskit_macos exposes it as AXCheckBox with AXToggle subrole.
A disclosure Poodle Button is present as AXButton with its AXTitle; AXExpanded is not listed by the current macOS element.
A mixed Poodle Checkbox is present as AXCheckBox with its AXTitle and an AXValue; the checked-versus-mixed distinction was not proven.
A Poodle Slider is present as AXSlider with its AXTitle, horizontal orientation, minimum 0, maximum 100, and value text 42.5 percent.
A selected AccessKit Tab is present as AXRadioButton with AXTabButton subrole and selected state in AXValue.
A disabled Button is present with AXEnabled false.
remainingLimits: Button A2 remains because the disclosure state was not exposed as AXExpanded.
Checkbox A2 remains because this proof did not distinguish the mixed state from checked in AXValue.
controls, labelled_by, and described_by string-ID relationships are not translated to AccessKit node IDs.
All other portable components retain A2 pending component-specific live platform evidence.

evidence: Accessible naming, validation-state exposure, check state, overlay dismissal posture, initial-focus posture, and focus-ring token resolution are explicit in the public primitive API.

The crate test surface already covers validation exposure, checked state exposure, dismiss-on-backdrop rules, popover initial focus, and focus ring tokens rather than leaving those semantics implicit.
remainingBlockers: Mounted native focus-scope ownership and focus restoration still need runnable GPUI review coverage.
Assistive-technology traces for dialog, menu, tabs, and selection widgets still require native runtime evidence rather than spec-only proof.

evidence: Validation summary and remediation composites expose announcement urgency explicitly through shared announcement modes instead of hiding that behavior in browser-only live regions.
Browse, detail, picker, selection-summary, and media composite specs keep labels, variant posture, empty or error states, and visible selection semantics explicit for later mounted GPUI review.
remainingBlockers: Structured table narration, picker active-item narration, and media fallback narration still need mounted native proof.
Composite shells do not yet ship a runnable GPUI review app section for every browse, detail, picker, and media route, so assistive-technology evidence remains manual.

evidence: Command and workstation shells already expose accessible labels, active-surface identity, command shortcut posture, grouped action meaning, and keyboard-resize capability explicitly in the public API.

The workstation crate test surface covers command discovery grouping, workspace identity, split keyboard-resize posture, and snapshot stability so shell meaning does not depend on undocumented runtime behavior.
remainingBlockers: Native dock focus scopes, focus recovery after command execution or overlay close, and named-region traversal still require mounted GPUI evidence.
Menu-bar ownership, multi-window movement, and downstream shell assistive-technology traces remain later runtime proof work.
Mounted field, text-entry, and validation-summary review surfaces are still required before native assistive-technology conformance can be promoted beyond manual proof.
Native table narration, row selection narration, and sort-state exposure still need mounted GPUI evidence.
Browse-shell focus order, filter recovery, and loading or result-count announcement posture remain native runtime review work.
Metadata narration, action ordering, and companion-pane traversal still need mounted native verification.
Modal or popover focus containment, active-item narration, and close recovery still require mounted GPUI proof.
Media playback, document preview, and unavailable-preview fallback narration remain the most runtime-specific accessibility debt in the current GPUI surface.
Native toast timing, queue narration, and escalation between polite and assertive announcement posture still need mounted evidence.
Modal command focus recovery, active-result narration, and execution feedback traces remain native review work.
Dock-region naming, multi-panel traversal, and layout-change narration still require mounted GPUI shell evidence.

manualReviewExpectations: Mounted GPUI review surfaces must still be exercised for focus entry, focus recovery, keyboard traversal, and announcement quality before any section can be promoted from manual proof to explicit assistive-technology conformance.
Cross-runtime comparison follows the screen-level comparison modes in packages/shared-demo-app-contract.json.
Native assistive-technology traces should capture real focus movement, announcement timing, and shell-region naming rather than relying on browser inference.
deltaRegister: Poodle's GPUI backend maps direct node roles, names, states, and values into AccessKit; ID-based controls, labelled_by, and described_by relationships are not projected because the GPUI backend does not translate their shared string IDs to AccessKit node IDs. No platform content was verified because macOS Accessibility trust was unavailable to the AXUIElement probe. All GPUI census A2 holds remain. See docs/contracts/003-native-accessibility.md.
Browser live-region and semantic HTML behavior still does work automatically in Svelte that GPUI must reproduce with native accessible-tree and announcement plumbing.
Overlay, menu, command palette, and picker focus containment remain the highest-risk cross-runtime delta because browser focus-scope behavior does not transfer automatically to GPUI.
Structured table, media preview, and workstation shell narration remain more runtime-specific than direct-parity visual comparison alone can prove.
nonGoals: Do not treat this proof artifact as full native conformance certification for every GPUI surface.
Do not claim mounted assistive-technology proof for sections that still only have spec-level or crate-test evidence.
Do not reopen Loophole-specific DAW widget ownership under the banner of GPUI accessibility work.
